card.name: Subject word before a past-tense report
card.fires_on: A subject word such as I, She, cases or also, or a comma, where a past-tense verb about what happened or was done comes next. It appears in teaching notes, how-to posts and drug-label adverse-event reports.

modes.label: Author's own account
modes.description: I or She starts a description of what the teacher or writer did or said.
modes.example: First,<< I>> gave them a dataset (the 1

modes.label: Reported cases
modes.description: The word cases begins a statement that events have been observed or reported.
modes.example: Bradycardia has generally occurred within hours to days, but<< cases>> have been observed up to 2 weeks

modes.label: Added past use
modes.description: A word such as also or a comma leads into a past-tense statement about prior use or what developed.
modes.example: It was<< also>> used in a 4-week course at

card.writes: It pushes toward past-tense, already-happened wording (曾, 未曾) and away from hedged 'may/might' wording (可能).
card.plain: It marks the spot where the text is about to say what already happened or was done, not what might happen.
